Midnight clears upper eastern then western roadblocks. Civilians remain neutral and are neither attacked nor blocked by operators.
Kroos clears the lower eastern roadblock after artillery clearance; Steward later clears the western roadblock. Spot intercepts pursuing officers.
Fang blocks upper central; Kroos supplies initial damage, Ansel heals, and returning Steward clears armor.
Friston blocks lower central; Fang and Kroos shorten exposure. Ansel sustains the lane; returning Steward must kill remaining armor including #34.
Midnight owns upper outer through its last hostile clearance, with temporary extended Ansel coverage.
Spot owns lower outer, alternating damage with self-healing. Healing-mode damage is zero; retained enemies must remain within three-block capacity.

formation_structure.execution_semantics: Fixed actions only. Handoff requirements are assertions, not executable branches. Failure of an assertion invalidates dependent actions; it does not create a substitute deployment.

formation_structure.mortality_policy: No required death. An operator death may have contributed damage or blocking, but yields no refund and releases blocked enemies. No death-dependent redeploy is scheduled. An unexpected central death has no guaranteed substitute and invalidates the containment hypothesis.
formation_structure.validation_status: UNSIMULATED; no shell commands, file mutations, simulations or other AI providers used.

revised_operational_plans.tactical_thesis: Restore early Kroos damage before medical expenditure, retain four ground interceptions, separate Steward from Ansel, and reserve Spot healing for the exposed medical window. After artillery clearance, rotate ranged output through armor and roadblock duties. This is a complete, unsimulated CURRENT_MODEL_CHECKABLE hypothesis; protected-target survival until artillery clearance remains its principal unresolved risk.

revised_stage_understanding.causal_revision: V4's cheap medic was affordable but displaced required opening damage. Its failure was exposure and survival, not arithmetic. V5 restores Kroos before medical spending and changes the Ansel/Steward geometry and Spot healing window. Neither change is presented as a demonstrated WIN.

evidence_boundaries.GameData: Catalog stats, legal terrain, source routes, skills and spawn definitions.
evidence_boundaries.UNKNOWN: Exact client timing, complete splash geometry, arbitrary targeting ties and ordinary navigation around active devices.
evidence_boundaries.USER_CONFIRMED_TACTICAL_PREMISE: Attack occupation can justify baiting or sacrifice when the specific observable behavior supports it; it does not establish pre-swing target lock.
evidence_boundaries.current_model: Action execution, ordinary attacks, supported skills, neutral civilians, roadblock restraint and delayed fixed-point artillery splash.

candidates.bait_or_sacrifice: None required; ordinary blocking consumes completed enemy attacks without assuming pre-swing lock. Retreats occur after asserted clearance, so no released enemy is intentionally transferred.
candidates.most_dangerous_window: Before Ansel arrives, Friston depends on kills rather than healing. Later, artillery may kill protected targets before sufficient eastern contact; separation does not solve target selection.

candidates.replaceability_assessment: Fang's economy and adjacent damage are both used. Friston's low cost buys early Kroos but leaves a survival liability. Kroos replaces Lancet because shortening exposure is currently more valuable than 70-ATK healing. Midnight combines outer damage and device reach. Spot replaces a separate lower medic. Ansel supplies broad central coverage. Steward supplies armor/artillery arts. Each duty could be substituted only with a newly funded geometry and timing calculation.
candidates.same_phase_responsibilities: Four ground interceptions, Kroos central damage, Ansel primary medical support, Steward artillery damage. Spot fuses blocking with periodic healing.
candidates.selection_reason: Best direct repair of the verified failure chain within seven IDs and existing executable actions. Selection is comparative, not a claim that protected survival or the later damage gap is proven.
candidates.staged_responsibilities: Steward rotates from artillery to armor to western lower restraint. Kroos rotates from central damage to eastern lower restraint. Midnight rotates from upper interception to western upper restraint.

bait_details.decoy_survival: Yato must survive until a completed strike if cooldown consumption is to be established by current rules. Retreating before ATTACK_STRIKE does not establish that consumption.
bait_details.enemy_and_attack: Lower-central enemy_1108_uterer ordinary melee attack; later enemy_1112_emppnt artillery ability.
bait_details.refund_and_redeploy: A living first Yato retreat refunds3 DP under the supplied half-cost model; death refunds0. Supported redeploy reduction gives40 seconds off field. Subsequent cost must follow inspected runtime behavior, not an assumed cheap reset.
bait_details.residual_risk: Yato retreat releases the trooper immediately. A born projectile remains dangerous at its locked point. Civilian promotion can defeat the desired artillery selection.
bait_details.successor: There is no spare eighth blocker. A lower-central successor would require moving Spot away from lower outer; that move has a 70-second cooldown and leaves another corridor vacant.

Also record released enemies, missing refund, lost role and real redeploy delay. A useful death is not automatically forbidden, but no death here has a guaranteed successor.

Do Fang's three required grants occur before dependent deployments?

Can the central blockers survive the post-artillery ranged rotation and retain every armor unit until Steward returns?
Are all four roadblocks destroyed and both safe arrivals explicitly observed?
